## Summary

Closed the scenario-4 cost basis and fixed the set size. crisperflow priced at 23.16 dollars per opus P session and waylla at 16.60, completing all six hosts: the floor is 5,304.60 dollars for 300 sessions at the old N=50 reference, 300 of 300 priced, so D20's gap line is gone and 4.0 is done. Two things the measurements overturned. M5's claim that cost tracks repo weight is only half right and the repo-weight half does not survive — waylla is a 59-file marketing site that cost more than the whole sofar engine, on more assistant turns and more tool calls than either crisperflow or sofar, so turn count is the mechanism and it is set by how much work the prompt invites rather than by how big the repo is. And every measurement moved the floor UP inside its own bracket, never down, closing above the earlier low end — the opposite of the scenario-3 experience where brillo's projected share collapsed as gaps filled, so unmeasured hosts should not be assumed cheap. With the basis closed, fixed N at 60 as D32, over the cheaper N=50, because n at least 150 needs 4.5 times N times spring to clear 150, which makes N=50 tolerate a spring rate of exactly the assumed 0.667 with no margin at all, and the failure is unrecoverable since nothing may be added afterwards. N=60 tolerates 0.556 for 1,178 dollars more. Allocation puts the cheaper large host at the cap: sofar 24, brillo 22, and the four small hosts at their full initiative supply.
